$comment: Findings the analyzer keeps flagging that we have decided NOT to act on. Each entry is a documented decision, not a hidden bug. New entries require a paired commit explaining the rationale.

suppressions.rationale: Per OPTIMIZATION_HANDOFF.md §Phase F: defer storage promotion. encryptedTvls is a strategy-level aggregate; in DeFi-scale lending pools the TVL of a popular strategy can easily exceed 2^63 wei (18.4 ETH at 18 decimals). The 25% gas saving is not worth the silent-overflow risk. Re-open if a runtime bound check `require(amount < (1 << 63))` is acceptable in the privacy model.

Per OPTIMIZATION_HANDOFF.md §Phase F: defer. supplyBalances stores per-user balances across all supported tokens. WETH at 18 decimals overflows euint64 above 18.4 ETH — a hard ceiling that would silently break for any non-trivial whale user. Real-chain risk dominates the 25% gas saving.

Per OPTIMIZATION_HANDOFF.md §Phase F: defer. Same overflow profile as F-05 — borrowBalances is per-user and shares the 18.4-ETH ceiling for 18-decimal tokens. Implementation would require a per-token decimal-aware storage strategy, deferred until product gives a concrete answer on the supported-token roadmap.

Per OPTIMIZATION_HANDOFF.md §Phase C: getBorrowBalance and getSupplyBalance read different mappings. A `mapping(address=>euint128) storage` parameter helper IS technically possible but the savings are ~64 bytes deployment-only and adding a function call to a hot read path risks losing internal-function inlining for a measurable runtime regression. Net trade is not worth the structural change.

Not a fix — this finding is the analyzer's structural map of `composer.openLeveragedStrategy` sub-step costs and exists to guide priority of OTHER findings. It cannot be "closed" by code changes. Its rendered table updates automatically as the code evolves; suppression here just declutters the open-findings list.
